passage:
Mr Nair walked in with the marked papers and said, "Two of you copied on the last question. I want to know who." Nobody breathed. I glanced at Ujjwal, who sits beside me. He stared at his desk and did not say a word, and neither did anyone else. After the bell the whole class was whispering names in the corridor, but Ujjwal didn't join in. He stayed behind. I saw him talking quietly with Mr Nair by the window for a few minutes. I don't know what they said, and Ujjwal didn't tell me. Nobody was called out in class. I can't say what he was feeling, but he looked tired when he came out.

Kishore

qa.q: What did Mr Nair say when he came in with the marked papers?
qa.a: That two of them copied on the last question and he wanted to know who.

qa.q: What could Kishore tell about Ujjwal's feelings, and what stayed unknown?
qa.a: Ujjwal looked tired afterwards, which suggests the situation weighed on him, but Kishore can't know his thoughts or what was said.

qa.q: Why was Ujjwal's way of handling the question wise?
qa.a: He did not gossip or lie outright, and he spoke to the teacher privately, weighing fairness to honest students against loyalty.

qa.q: How might the honest students in the class see what happened?
qa.a: Possibly with relief that the matter went to the teacher, since fairness matters to them. Nobody was named in class, so they may also feel unsure.

grounding: A teacher asks who cheated; the protagonist avoids gossip and speaks privately with the teacher, seen by an observer.

passage:
Wednesday, 9:40 pm

Today Rekha ma'am held up two history papers with the exact same wrong date and said, "I know some of you know who shared. Whoever it is, come and see me." Then silence, the kind where you can hear the fan.

I know it was Aman and Dev. Dev showed me the photos before the test and I said no. I felt my ears go hot the whole time she was talking.

At lunch the gossip started. Everyone had a theory, and someone asked me straight out. I said, "I'm not discussing it here." That felt right. Spreading names in the canteen would just be another kind of unfair.

But the honest kids who studied got the same suspicious look from ma'am as everyone. That isn't fair either. So after the last bell I went to the staffroom and told her quietly what I saw, just the facts. I didn't enjoy it. My hands were shaking.

Siddharth

qa.q: What did the two history papers have in common?
qa.a: The two history papers had the exact same wrong date.

qa.q: What was Siddharth feeling while Rekha ma'am was talking?
qa.a: Siddharth felt tense and uncomfortable, with hot ears, because of knowing who had shared answers and not yet deciding what to do.

qa.q: Which choice worked better than gossiping, and why?
qa.a: Speaking quietly to Rekha ma'am in the staffroom worked better, because it was fair to the students who studied without spreading names around the canteen.

qa.q: How might Rekha ma'am see Siddharth coming to the staffroom?
qa.a: She may feel relieved to get honest facts, and see Siddharth as someone who cared about fairness enough to come even with shaking hands. 🙏

grounding: It shows a teen asked by a teacher about cheating who weighs fairness against loyalty, refuses to gossip and speaks to the teacher privately.
